1.explanation:
All of these files participate in rendering the MultiSelect’s outer field and its interactive children:
• ListBoxField.js is the component that renders the selection container as a <button> (with role="button"). 
• ListBoxSelection.js drives how each selected item is turned into an interactive pill by wrapping the Tag component. 
• MultiSelect.js (and FilterableMultiSelect.js) instantiate ListBoxField/ListBoxSelection to manage the selected items and the clear‐selection UI. 
• Tag.js (the “filter” tag variant) renders its own <button> (or role=“button”) for each pill’s close icon. 
Together, this nesting of interactive containers leads to a <button> element containing other interactive descendants, which directly causes the reported accessibility violation and must be refactored (for example, by not using a <button> for the parent ListBoxField in multi‐select mode or by rendering selection pills with non-<button> wrappers).
1.bug_scenario: When one or more items are selected in the MultiSelect dropdown, the component renders the entire selection‐display area using an interactive container (a “button” element via ListBoxField). Inside of that container it then injects the selected–item pills (ListBoxSelection) which themselves are interactive (they use Tag filter variant that renders its own <button> or role=“button”). In effect you end up with a nested button (or a button with interactive descendants), which both a) produces accessibility errors (screen readers/keyboard users see confusing nested controls) and b) violates the HTML5 spec requirement that “there must be no interactive content descendant” inside a <button>. The two screenshots in the bug report highlight the nested controls (a button with inner role=button/filter tags) and the visual pills in the UI.

2.explanation:
• ListBoxField.js: Renders the outer wrapper of the dropdown as a native <button type="button">. Changing this to a non-button element (e.g. <div role="button">) or conditionally dropping ‘type="button"’ for the multiselect prevents nested <button>s.

• ListBoxSelection.js: Inside the list-box field the selected-item tags are rendered via <button> (the Tag’s remove control). That inner <button> is the interactive descendant of the ListBoxField’s <button>.

• MultiSelect.js: References ListBoxField/ListBoxSelection via the ListBox API; adjustments here (or in the FilterableMultiSelect wrapper) ensure that for the multiselect variant the outer container is not a <button> when tags are present.

By updating ListBoxField.js (and, as needed, the MultiSelect wrapper) to use a non-button container for the field, or switching the tag-remove control to a non-<button> element, we eliminate the nested interactive content violation.
2.bug_scenario: When one or more items are selected in the Carbon MultiSelect, the control renders its root list-box field as a <button> and each selected item as a tag with its own remove <button>. This results in a <button> containing interactive descendants (other <button>s), which violates the W3C spec “there must be no interactive content descendant” and creates accessibility errors.
